h: Tee Off Tips and the City Around You
p: Going in a big group? Splitting into smaller teams is a good shout, as it keeps everyone involved rather than waiting ages for their turn on each hole. It can actually add to the fun, as you get a mini competition within the main competition. Turn up a little before your tee time to grab a drink and get everyone sorted.

Remember it's crazy golf, not the Open. Nobody's judging your swing, and the best moments usually come from the most ridiculous misses. If someone in your group takes it too seriously, that's half the entertainment for everyone else.

Manchester is the perfect place to build a night out around a round of golf. Spinningfields is packed with stylish bars and restaurants, while Ancoats has become one of the city's best spots for food, with independent bakeries, cafés and restaurants in converted mills. Chinatown, with its grand archway, is great for a pre-golf feed.

If you've got time during the day, Salford Quays is a short tram ride away, with IWM North, the Lowry arts centre and MediaCityUK all by the water. The Manchester Museum on Oxford Road is free and has dinosaurs, Egyptian artefacts and a vivarium full of frogs and lizards, making it a great add-on for a daytime trip.
